summary: Failed-verdict terminal states: every failed executor verdict ends in a repair (re-queued or delivered), a timeboxed Decision Catalog entry, or an operator notification; route-to-planner is not a terminal state and mechanical repairs never route to a model session

options.description: Invariant checked by the tick: a failed verdict ends in (i) repaired and re-queued or delivered, (ii) a timeboxed catalog entry with autonomous fallback, or (iii) an operator notification with a deadline; the playbook finishes a repaired push (verify, mark ready, delivered verdict); a stuck signed PR opens a stall that escalates and notifies; route-to-planner ages. Implemented by AISDLC-1156 (dispatch) and AISDLC-1154 (Step 11 fast-forward fallback).

Keep route-to-planner as the terminal state and make the planner session a polling loop that acts on routed PRs autonomously. Rejected: spends model turns on deterministic repairs, and the planner is deliberately not a loop (RFC-0051 section 7).
Keep the current states and add a desktop notification on every aged PR. Rejected: still a human in the loop for a mechanical repair; the notification is the fallback of option one, not a substitute.

body: Incidents: AISDLC-1136 (#2246, 2026-11-01) and AISDLC-1153 (#2282, 2026-11-02) passed verify, review and signing, failed only the final push (stale resume lease on a fast-forward), and sat as unowned drafts for hours until the operator noticed. Trace: the playbook repairs but never re-queues, marks ready or writes a delivered verdict; route-to-planner runs no command, is exempt from aging and sends one deduped message (none for #2282); drain-stall and human-attention do not cover a stuck PR; stall-notice is never called. RFC-0051 section 8 says the planner is asked only for design questions, and a human only for Open Questions in substance; a mechanical push failure is neither. Operator ruling 2026-11-02: a pipeline that depends on a human noticing a failure is a workflow failure.
